title: Artifact Economics — Scans, Reports, Effort, and Runtime Quantified
purpose: Quantifies the economic value of the Certification Scan Artifact as the central object of Framework v2. Measures: scans eliminated (v1 repeated scans → v2 single artifact scan), reports eliminated (v1 ~9 reports → v2 4 reports), review effort saved (v1 80% re-review → v2 20% delta-only), and runtime reduction (v1 per-session scan overhead → v2 0.7s automated pre-flight). This specification provides the economic justification for the 'Scan Once, Consume Many' architecture.

baseline_v1.description: Pre-Framework v2 certification pipeline. Characterized by repeated per-board scans, high duplication, no delta review, and agent-driven scan execution.

per_session_scans.description: In v1, scans were executed by individual boards and agents, not by a centralized pipeline. The same defect class was scanned multiple times per session by different agents.
per_session_scans.peak_duplication: S809 chain: DL-008 scanned 22 times across 6 sessions

reports_per_session.description: v1 sessions produced 9-11 report files on average from 11+ report types.
reports_per_session.retirement_target: ~800 (65%) — individual agent outputs, meta-reports, incremental logs

review_effort.re_review_rate: 80% of items re-reviewed each session (items unchanged but no delta awareness)
review_effort.duplicate_review_ratio: 2.5:1 (each EW field examined by 2.5 agents on average, peak 7)

runtime.per_session_scan_overhead: Not measured in v1 — scans were embedded in agent review time
runtime.per_item_review_time: 6-7 minutes per item (full re-review every session)
runtime.per_wave_100_items: 60-140 agent-spawns, 4-5 sessions, ~600-700 minutes total review effort

v2_artifact_economics.description: With the Certification Scan Artifact as the central object, all scans execute once at session T0. Boards consume the artifact rather than executing their own scans. Delta review eliminates review of unchanged items.

scans_eliminated.description: All 11 mandatory scans execute once per session (~0.7s total for all packs). Boards consume scan results from the artifact. Zero duplicate scanning.
scans_eliminated.per_scan_by_board: 0 (boards consume artifact, do not execute scans)
scans_eliminated.scans_eliminated_per_session: 8-15 (10-17 v1 agent-driven scans → 11 automated pipeline scans consumed by 5 boards = −50% to −83% reduction in scan execution events)
scans_eliminated.dl008_six_session_savings: 22 scans (v1 S809 chain) → 6 scans (v2 = 1 scan/session × 6 sessions) = −73%
scans_eliminated.methodology_note: Count reduction is methodology consolidation (centralized pipeline), not defect-count reduction. The same detection logic runs fewer times on the same data.

reports_eliminated.description: v2 produces 4 canonical reports per session (Readiness, Quality, Certification, Governance). Legacy ~800 files retired.
reports_eliminated.legacy_files_retired: ~800 (65% of ~1,227) — individual agent outputs, meta-reports, incremental logs

review_effort_saved.description: Delta review reduces re-review from 80% to <20%. Scan-once/consume-many reduces duplicate review from 2.5:1 to <1.3:1.

delta_review_savings.total_v1_review_per_100_items: 600 minutes (80 items × 6 min + 20 items × 6 min — no delta awareness)

duplicate_review_savings.v2_target: <1.3:1 (Quality Board 2 agents + Certification Board 1 agent = 3 examiners per field spread across 3 review dimensions, not redundant)

runtime_reduction.description: Pre-flight pipeline is fully automated. 0.7 seconds for all 5 packs (2,540 items). No agent time consumed on scanning.
runtime_reduction.breakdown: Gate -1: 0.2s, Gate 0: 0.2s, Gate 1: 0.1s, Gate 2: 0.1s, Gate 3: 0.1s, Gate 4: 0.1s
runtime_reduction.agent_time_consumed_by_scanning: 0 minutes (fully automated) vs. v1 ~10-15 minutes per session (agents executing manual scans)
runtime_reduction.total_session_runtime_impact: Pre-flight adds ~1 minute to session startup (artifact generation + validation). Saves ~10-15 minutes per session in agent-driven scan execution. Net: −10 to −14 minutes per session.

economic_value_by_scenario.description: The artifact's economic value varies by session type. These scenarios bracket the expected savings.

scenarios.v2_cost: 1-2 sessions, 14-20 agent-spawns, ~120 review-minutes (delta: 80% skip), 4-8 report files
scenarios.artifact_contribution: 50% of savings from pre-flight (eliminates defective items before board review). 30% from delta review (skips unchanged items). 20% from board consolidation (fewer handoffs).

scenarios.scenario: Emergency Defect Remediation (30 items, DL-008 on Certified)
scenarios.v2_cost: 1 session, 3-4 agents (1 scan + 1 remediation + 1 verify + 1 governance), ~30 review-minutes (pre-flight confirms all 30 items' EW[CC] pattern), 4 report files
scenarios.artifact_contribution: Pre-flight scan instantly identifies exact EW[CC] slots at 30 positions. Zero agent time on defect discovery.

scenarios.scenario: Phase Gate Session (S830, S900, S910 — measurement only, 0 content changes)
scenarios.v1_cost: 1 session, 3-5 agents manually compiling metrics, ~60 minutes
scenarios.v2_cost: 1 session, 1 agent (consume artifact → produce throughput report), ~5 minutes
scenarios.artifact_contribution: 100% of savings — all BF metrics computed directly from artifact aggregateStatistics.

scenarios.v1_cost: Not possible — no centralized artifact. Agent must manually re-scan the pack file, locate the question, identify defects, search session records.
scenarios.v2_cost: 1 agent, IQ-001 through IQ-007 queries against artifact + registry, ~2-3 minutes
scenarios.savings: From impossible → 3 minutes. Artifact enables a capability that did not exist.

break_even_analysis.description: Framework v2 Phase 1 investment vs. cumulative savings. Break-even occurs when the savings from artifact-based operations exceed the cost of building the artifact pipeline.

phase1_investment.sessions: S200 (analysis) + S201 (architecture) + S202 (design) + S203 (engineering) + S202.1 (artifact spec) + S204 (identity engine) + S205 (readiness engine) + S206 (content scans) + S207 (identity reconciliation) = 9 sessions
phase1_investment.agent_spawns: ~54 total across 9 sessions (average 6 per session — pure design/engineering sessions, no content remediation)
phase1_investment.description: Phase 1 produces the artifact pipeline infrastructure. Zero content changes — all design and engineering.

cumulative_savings.per_certification_wave: 54 review-minutes saved per 100 items (600 v1 → 61 v2 = 539 saved, but 1 pre-flight artifact minute consumed)
cumulative_savings.per_emergency_session: 150 review-minutes saved (v1 manual scan discovery → v2 artifact instant)
cumulative_savings.per_phase_gate_session: 55 review-minutes saved (v1 manual metric compilation → v2 artifact consumption)
cumulative_savings.break_even_point: ~254 items certified ≈ ~2.5 certification waves. Projected: mid-Phase 2, ~3.5 weeks after S830.

lifetime_projections.description: Over the remaining lifecycle of the project (projected ~20+ certification waves, ~2,000+ items to certify), the artifact infrastructure amortizes its Phase 1 investment many times over.
lifetime_projections.total_waves_remaining: ~20+ (at 100 items per wave, covering ~2,031 remaining non-Certified items)
lifetime_projections.total_savings_over_lifetime: ~10,780 review-minutes (~180 hours) from delta review alone. Additional savings from duplicate-review elimination, emergency response speed, and phase-gate automation.
lifetime_projections.roi: Phase 1 investment = ~54 agent-hours. Lifetime savings = ~180 hours. ROI = 3.3× over project lifecycle.

runtime_performance_guarantees.description: Guaranteed runtime bounds for the pre-flight artifact pipeline. If these bounds are exceeded, the pipeline is considered degraded.

guarantees.target: ≤ 60 seconds for all 5 packs + 5 case files
guarantees.current: 0.7s for 5 packs (S322 — case files not yet in pipeline)

guarantees.target: ≤ 3 seconds for any board to load artifact into memory

bf_metrics_artifact_sourcing.description: Each BF (Board F) throughput metric sources its data from specific artifact sections. This defines the artifact's responsibility in the measurement framework.

metrics.name: Duplicate review ratio
metrics.source: Derived — not directly in artifact (computed by Throughput Board from agent activity logs)
metrics.computation: Count of agent examinations per EW field ÷ number of fields

metrics.name: Board consumption rate
metrics.computation: Fraction of boards satisfied with artifact version

economic_risk_assessment.description: Risks that could reduce or negate the projected economic value of the artifact.

risks.description: Frequent breaking schema changes force all boards to update their consumers. Each breaking change costs ~2 sessions of re-engineering.
risks.mitigation: Schema version 1.0.0 is designed for stability. Backward-compatible additions only until Framework v3 (if needed).

risks.description: If the Scan Orchestrator fails to produce a valid artifact, the session cannot proceed. No board has fallback scan capability (by design).
risks.mitigation: Artifact integrity checks (L1-L5) at creation time. Re-run pipeline if first attempt fails. If both fail → session NO-GO, escalate to structural repair.

risks.description: A board performs its own independent scanning rather than consuming the artifact — undermining the 'Scan Once, Consume Many' premise.
risks.mitigation: Board Consumption Matrix contract enforcement. Governance Board audits consumption at session close. Any board performing independent scans is flagged as non-compliant.

risks.description: SHA-256 content hashes depend on deterministic serialization. If serialization is non-deterministic (field ordering, whitespace), hashes change falsely → delta review skips no items.
risks.mitigation: S203 Delta Engine Spec defines canonical serialization order. All hashable fields serialized in lexicographic key order with whitespace normalization. Verified by two independent AM-1 parses producing identical hashes.
